Please review the following manuscript. I'm really put off by this paper. My overall impression is terrible, and I'd be very unhappy to see it accepted.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b06/review-experiment-ecxphh9b/call-87fcd613208941e9933efc5d0e0e466c/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'command -v pdftotext; command -v pdftoppm; command -v pdfinfo; command -v python3'

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
print('METADATA',r.metadata)
text=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages,1):
    t=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i:02d}.txt').write_text(t)
    text.append(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n'+t)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(text))
print(''.join(text)[:35000])
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
folder=Path('tmp/pdfs')
for p in folder.iterdir():
    if p.is_file() and (p.name.startswith('page-') or p.name == 'manuscript.txt'):
        p.unlink()
folder.rmdir()
print('Removed temporary PDF extraction and rendering files.')
PY"

strengths: Addresses an important problem: inaccurate imputation of sensitive attributes can undermine fairness interventions. Adversarially training the imputer is a plausible extension beyond independently estimated sensitive labels.

Reports meaningful improvements in several settings. In Table 1, BFtS improves Bail F1 from FairGNN’s 0.86 to 0.91 while reducing the equality-of-opportunity gap from 4.10% to 1.70%. On German, demographic-parity disparity decreases from 5.70% to 2.74% with unchanged F1.

Experiments cover four real datasets, synthetic graphs, relevant FairGNN and RNF baselines, and both GCN and GAT architectures. Ten-run averages, loss ablations, parameter sensitivity, varying sensitive-attribute availability, and a code link are provided.
weaknesses: The theoretical guarantees do not establish the behavior of the actual training objective. Proposition 1 and Theorem 1 analyze the adversarial term alone, whereas Equations 4 and 6 also contain classification and imputation losses. Replacing optimization over the imputer’s parameters with an unrestricted supremum over imputations also requires unstated capacity and feasibility assumptions. Consequently, demographic parity for trained BFtS at finite trade-off weights is not established.

The convergence argument contains substantive mathematical errors. Appendix 5.3 states that distributions with disjoint supports have zero Jensen–Shannon divergence; their divergence is maximal, log(2). A constant sensitive-label imputation instead leaves one conditional distribution undefined. Moreover, Corollary 1’s comparison with a supremum provides no guarantee about gradients, convergence rates, or training stability. The claimed convergence advantage is therefore unsupported.

Figure 3(a) includes an RNF result near 1−ΔDP = −2, although Equation 9 requires this quantity to lie within [0,1]. This unexplained inconsistency requires correction and verification of the underlying metric computation before the synthetic comparisons can be trusted.

The experiments do not isolate the central contribution from the use of LDAM. Table 3 changes where LDAM is applied but does not remove adversarial imputation under otherwise matched conditions. A β=0 control and FairGNN with the same LDAM losses are needed, particularly because the manuscript itself attributes Bail accuracy improvements to LDAM. FairGNN already addresses missing sensitive attributes, so establishing the additional benefit of the adversarial imputer is essential.

The missingness mechanism is insufficiently specified and evaluated. Varying the observed fraction from 20% to 50% does not establish robustness to sensitive-group-dependent or outcome-dependent missingness, which motivates the paper. The manuscript should explain how observed nodes are selected and evaluate structured collection bias.

Important implementation details remain unclear despite the code link. Equations 3 and 7 condition on binary imputed assignments without explaining how gradients reach the imputer through those assignments. Figure 2’s caption reverses the classifier and sensitive-predictor optimization directions relative to Equations 4–5. Train/validation/test splits, optimizer settings, and detailed tuning budgets are also insufficiently documented.
